title.narrative: Advancing Green Investment and Resilient Economic Growth Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative:
The program supports the Kyrgyz Republic's ambitious reform agenda to accelerate climate action, attract sustainable investment, and transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. It aims to (i) strengthen climate-aligned policies, coordination, and institutional arrangements; (ii) enhance the enabling environment for mobilizing public and private finance for climate action; and (iii) strengthen adaptation priorities and resilience to climate impacts. Subprogram 1 ($50 million), implemented from January 2024 to September 2025, established the foundation for new regulations, sector programs, initiatives, and institutional frameworks. Subprogram 2 ($50 million), scheduled from September 2025 to June 2027, will continue and expand operationalization of the frameworks that have been adopted. These integrated fiscal, financial, and institutional reforms aim to reduce climate-induced economic vulnerabilities, improve public financial management (PFM), and unlock investment opportunities.
The program's impact is aligned with the National Development Strategy of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2018-2040 and the National Development Program of Kyrgyz Republic until 2030 to provide better economic opportunities for citizens through sustainable, inclusive, and resilient economic growth. The program outcome is climate action, investment, and the green economy transition accelerated. The program will create a coherent and effective institutional setup, mobilize climate finance, and develop adaptation priorities to strengthen the country's economic resilience to climate change. Crosscutting issues of gender and social inclusion are addressed together with improved standards, environmental management, and support to regional cooperation and integration. Strengthened institutions and policies will drive more climate investments, open new sectors for growth, and support a resilient, low-carbon green economy, resulting in higher and sustainable growth.

Reform area: Public and private climate finance mobilization enhanced.
Outcome: By 2028, the share of banks' green loans to the total lending portfolio increased to 1%.
Description: To enhance the integration and adoption of sustainable finance principles into the banking sector and nonbank finance institutions (NBFIs), the National Bank of Kyrgyz Republic (NBKR): (i) Approved the roadmap on the development of sustainable finance and the implementation of ESG principles in the banking sector of the Kyrgyz Republic; (ii) Established requirements for banks to disclose sustainability-related information in accordance with international standards through regulation 'On Minimum Requirements to the Code of Corporate Governance for Commercial Banks of the Kyrgyz Republic'; (iii) Issued recommendations for banks and NBFIs to integrate ESG reporting and develop sustainable financing mechanisms to enhance transparency and promote responsible investment practices; and (iv) Issued requirements for banks to remotely identify and verify individuals using client data received in electronic form, without the need for personal presence, to ensure equal access to financial services and address disability and incorporating gender-specific needs through amendment to the rules “On clients remote identification and verification”.

Reform area: Public and private climate finance mobilization enhanced.
Outcome: By 2028, the share of banks' green loans to the total lending portfolio increased to 1%.
Description: To facilitate the mobilization of green and climate finance and enhance the reliability and comparability of information on sustainability risks and opportunities, the government approved a medium term Road Map for Implementation of Sustainable Financial Reporting covering major public entities (large listed entities, joint-stock state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and including banks) to adopt sustainability disclosure standards comprising of International Financial Reporting Standard Sustainability Disclosure Standards (IFRS-S1) on sustainability-related financial disclosures; and IFSR-S2 on climate-related disclosures.

Reform area: Public and private climate finance mobilization enhanced.
Outcome: By 2028, the share of banks' green loans to the total lending portfolio increased to 1%.
Description: To mobilize sovereign and non-sovereign green and sustainable financing instruments for climate change related projects: (i) The government approved an interministerial working group to develop a Sovereign Green Bond Framework that is aligned with international standards for sovereign bond issuances; and (ii) Amendments to the Law of the Kyrgyz Republic "On the Securities Market" were approved, incorporating provisions to support the issuance of green bonds, sustainability-linked bonds, sustainable development goals (SDG) bonds, and social bonds.

Reform area: Resilience to climate impacts strengthened.
Outcome: By 2028, $4 million green mortgages issued, of which 30% are allocated to women.
Description: To implement risk layering approach and to increase risk mitigation options for government liabilities and enhance protection cover against disasters triggered by natural hazards, the government: (i) Mandated state budget organizations and SOEs to obtain disaster insurance of assets on their balance sheets, and allocate sufficient financing in annual budgets to finance insurance premiums/cost to mitigate risks of disasters triggered by natural hazards; and (ii) Enforced a system of affordable compulsory insurance of residential premises against fire and natural disasters.

Reform area: Resilience to climate impacts strengthened.
Outcome: By 2028, $4 million green mortgages issued, of which 30% are allocated to women.
Description: To improve the efficiency of the civil protection system, timely prevention measures and ensuring readiness to respond to possible emergencies, prevent loss of life and reduce damages, the government mandated (a) allocation of funds in annual budgets for activities aimed at protecting the population and territories from emergencies; (b) implementation of measures to protect settlements and their infrastructure from mudflows and floods based on a comprehensive inventory; (c) revision of norms for staffing emergencies and specialized units at fuel and energy complex facilities; (d) creation of a system for monitoring the technological safety of industrial hazardous objects and hydraulic structures; and (e) long-term investments in green forest plantations in foothills and agroforestry in river floodplains to reduce flood and mudflow processes, erosion of banks, and land degradation.

Reform area: Resilience to climate impacts strengthened.
Outcome: By 2028, $4 million green mortgages issued, of which 30% are allocated to women.
Description: To promote resilience of national economy, rational and sustainable use of available natural resources to withstand climate shocks and introduce the latest international legal and regulatory practices: (i) The new Water Code unifying separate laws and improving water management was approved; (ii) The amendments to the Energy Savings Law; mandating efficient energy use, metering and accountability across public and private sectors was approved, and (iii) The government approved the establishment of an interministerial working group to develop the Renewable Energy Program, with gender considerations to support implementation of energy efficiency and green agenda.

Reform area: Resilience to climate impacts strengthened.
Outcome: By 2028, $4 million green mortgages issued, of which 30% are allocated to women.

Reform area: Climate-aligned policies, coordination and institutional arrangements strengthened
Outcome: By June 2028, the total volume of financing for green economy increased by 30% annually.
Description: To define a long-term cross-sectorial national strategy for low-carbon and climate-resilient development, and to attract international green investments through key priority sectors, the government approved: (i) the Concept on Achieving Carbon Neutrality by 2050 with gender-responsive approach and Phase 1 Implementation Action Plan (2025-2030); (ii) the National Green Taxonomy that sets out the common priorities and defines eligible green projects, goods, services activities and technology; and (iii) the Green Economy Development Program until 2029 defining key directions of green economy policies including proposed gender-responsive measures.

Reform area: Climate-aligned policies, coordination and institutional arrangements strengthened
Outcome: By June 2028, the total volume of financing for green economy increased by 30% annually.
Description: To establish a comprehensive climate information service, data production, and methodological framework to support economic planning: (i) The National Statistical Committee (NSC) approved (a) a set of national climate change and green economy indicators, and (b) a Roadmap on Enhancement of Climate Statistics to develop and formalize methodologies and operational framework to support climate data collection with relevant sex-disaggregation across five program areas of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), namely, impact factors, vulnerabilities, mitigation, and adaptation; (ii) MINRETS approved the development of Unified Climate Change Information Platform on its website to expand access by government agencies supporting climate change and green actions to enhance interagency information; and (iii) Hydrometeorological Service under Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) developed and shared its set of climate data with the NSC for further dissemination.

Reform area: Climate-aligned policies, coordination and institutional arrangements strengthened
Outcome: By June 2028, the total volume of financing for green economy increased by 30% annually.
Description: To strengthen interagency coordination, adopt a consolidated approach and clarify the roles and responsibilities of different agencies, the government: (i) unified multiple existing arrangements (committees, councils, working groups) under a single Coordination Council on Ecology, Climate Change and the Green Economy (Coordination Council) and an updated mandate for high-level decision making and coordination of all relevant agencies and regional authorities responsible for climate change actions (covering environmental, social, gender equality, economic, financial and sectoral aspects); and (ii) assigned government agencies as lead responsible government bodies for the Council (Deputy Chairpersons - Minister of Natural Resources, Ecology and Technical Supervision [MINRETS] and Minister of Economy and Commerce [MOEC]) and assigned the secretariat (Climate Finance Center under Cabinet of Ministers) to coordinate all relevant climate change agenda.

Reform area: Climate-aligned policies, coordination and institutional arrangements strengthened
Outcome: By June 2028, the total volume of financing for green economy increased by 30% annually.
Description: To support longer-term reform efforts and set up a system for accounting of green expenditures in the government budget, the government: (i) completed piloting of green budget tagging in 2 ministries in FY2024/2025 (MINRETS and MES), (ii) initiated phase 2 of green budget tagging pilot in 3 additional ministries (MOF, Ministry of Energy, and Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry) starting from FY2026, (iii) approved green budget tagging implementation roadmap for 2025-2027, and (iv) updated green budget tagging methodology.

Action 3: To establish a comprehensive climate information service, data production, and methodological framework to support economic planning: (i) The National Statistical Committee (NSC) approved (a) a set of national climate change and green economy indicators, and (b) a Roadmap on Enhancement of Climate Statistics to develop and formalize methodologies and operational framework to support climate data collection with relevant sex-disaggregation across five program areas of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), namely, impact factors, vulnerabilities, mitigation, and adaptation; (ii) MINRETS approved the development of Unified Climate Change Information Platform on its website to expand access by government agencies supporting climate change and green actions to enhance interagency information; and (iii) Hydrometeorological Service under Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) developed and shared its set of climate data with the NSC for further dissemination.
Action 4: To support longer-term reform efforts and set up a system for accounting of green expenditures in the government budget, the government: (i) completed piloting of green budget tagging in 2 ministries in FY2024/2025 (MINRETS and MES), (ii) initiated phase 2 of green budget tagging pilot in 3 additional ministries (MOF, Ministry of Energy, and Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry) starting from FY2026, (iii) approved green budget tagging implementation roadmap for 2025-2027, and (iv) updated green budget tagging methodology.

Action 1: To mobilize sovereign and non-sovereign green and sustainable financing instruments for climate change related projects: (i) The government approved an interministerial working group to develop a Sovereign Green Bond Framework that is aligned with international standards for sovereign bond issuances; and (ii) Amendments to the Law of the Kyrgyz Republic "On the Securities Market" were approved, incorporating provisions to support the issuance of green bonds, sustainability-linked bonds, sustainable development goals (SDG) bonds, and social bonds.
Action 2: To facilitate the mobilization of green and climate finance and enhance the reliability and comparability of information on sustainability risks and opportunities, the government approved a medium term Road Map for Implementation of Sustainable Financial Reporting covering major public entities (large listed entities, joint-stock state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and including banks) to adopt sustainability disclosure standards comprising of International Financial Reporting Standard Sustainability Disclosure Standards (IFRS-S1) on sustainability-related financial disclosures; and IFSR-S2 on climate-related disclosures.
Action 3: To enhance the integration and adoption of sustainable finance principles into the banking sector and nonbank finance institutions (NBFIs), the National Bank of Kyrgyz Republic (NBKR): (i) Approved the roadmap on the development of sustainable finance and the implementation of ESG principles in the banking sector of the Kyrgyz Republic; (ii) Established requirements for banks to disclose sustainability-related information in accordance with international standards through regulation 'On Minimum Requirements to the Code of Corporate Governance for Commercial Banks of the Kyrgyz Republic'; (iii) Issued recommendations for banks and NBFIs to integrate ESG reporting and develop sustainable financing mechanisms to enhance transparency and promote responsible investment practices; and (iv) Issued requirements for banks to remotely identify and verify individuals using client data received in electronic form, without the need for personal presence, to ensure equal access to financial services and address disability and incorporating gender-specific needs through amendment to the rules “On clients remote identification and verification”.

Action 1: To improve the efficiency of the civil protection system, timely prevention measures and ensuring readiness to respond to possible emergencies, prevent loss of life and reduce damages, the government mandated (a) allocation of funds in annual budgets for activities aimed at protecting the population and territories from emergencies; (b) implementation of measures to protect settlements and their infrastructure from mudflows and floods based on a comprehensive inventory; (c) revision of norms for staffing emergencies and specialized units at fuel and energy complex facilities; (d) creation of a system for monitoring the technological safety of industrial hazardous objects and hydraulic structures; and (e) long-term investments in green forest plantations in foothills and agroforestry in river floodplains to reduce flood and mudflow processes, erosion of banks, and land degradation.
Action 2: To implement risk layering approach and to increase risk mitigation options for government liabilities and enhance protection cover against disasters triggered by natural hazards, the government: (i) Mandated state budget organizations and SOEs to obtain disaster insurance of assets on their balance sheets, and allocate sufficient financing in annual budgets to finance insurance premiums/cost to mitigate risks of disasters triggered by natural hazards; and (ii) Enforced a system of affordable compulsory insurance of residential premises against fire and natural disasters.
Action 3: To strengthen resilience and competitiveness, and facilitate cross-border tourism development consistent with the Central Asia Regional Economic Corridor (CAREC) Tourism Strategy 2030, reduce greenhouse gas emission from cargo transportation on CAREC Corridor 2, and develop integrated regional mechanism for coordination and interaction among countries in CAREC region in mitigating challenges coming from climate change and implementing adaptation measures, the government: (i) Adopted a Sustainable Tourism Development Program for 2025-2030, including encompassing regions in mountainous and cross-border areas; (ii) Approved a joint roadmap to develop a cross-border sustainable tourism cluster with one other CAREC member country; (iii) Launched a pilot Electronic Queue Management System (eQMS) in at least one border crossing point along CAREC Corridor 2; and (iv) Approved the Regional Strategy of Climate Change Adaptation in Central Asia.
Action 4: To promote resilience of national economy, rational and sustainable use of available natural resources to withstand climate shocks and introduce the latest international legal and regulatory practices: (i) The new Water Code unifying separate laws and improving water management was approved; (ii) The amendments to the Energy Savings Law; mandating efficient energy use, metering and accountability across public and private sectors was approved, and (iii) The government approved the establishment of an interministerial working group to develop the Renewable Energy Program, with gender considerations to support implementation of energy efficiency and green agenda.
